title: SEC Targets Tokenization, AI and Quantum Computing in 2027 Examination Priorities
excerpt: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is putting tokenized securities, AI, and quantum computing under heightened scrutiny.
content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is putting tokenized securities, artificial intelligence, and quantum computing under heightened scrutiny as the technologies increasingly reshape financial markets, according to its newly released fiscal year 2027 examination priorities.

Key Takeaways

  • The SEC named tokenized securities as an examination priority, focusing on clearing agencies and market infrastructure resilience.
  • Regulators will scrutinize AI-powered trading, investment advice, cybersecurity threats, deepfakes, and compliance systems.
  • The SEC flagged quantum computing as an emerging concern but stopped short of specifying risks to cryptocurrencies or mandating quantum-resistant safeguards.

The SEC Targets Tokenization in 2027

The SEC’s Division of Examinations identified the three technologies among emerging trends that will inform its oversight of regulated financial institutions, including clearing agencies, securities exchanges, broker-dealers, and investment advisers.

Tokenization, which involves representing traditional financial assets such as stocks and bonds as digital tokens on blockchain networks, appears in two separate sections of the report.

Under its clearing agency priorities, the SEC said examinations will focus on high-risk areas including default management, securities lending, operational controls, and tokenization. Clearing agencies play a critical role in processing and settling securities transactions, making their technological reliability essential to market stability.

The regulator also identified tokenized securities as an emerging concern under Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity (SCI), which establishes operational resilience and technology safeguards for certain key market participants.

“Examinations under Regulation SCI will focus on emerging trends, including [AI], tokenization of securities, extended trading hours, and quantum computing,” the report states.

The references come as traditional financial institutions increasingly explore blockchain technology to modernize securities trading, settlement and asset management.

However, the SEC stopped short of outlining specific new requirements for tokenized assets, and notably did not establish separate examination priorities for cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, or decentralized finance.

AI Takes Center Stage

Artificial intelligence received substantially greater attention throughout the report, although the SEC repeatedly referred to the technology as “super intelligence,” or SI.

The regulator acknowledged that financial institutions are increasingly deploying advanced AI systems for investment analysis, portfolio management, customer communications, software development, and regulatory compliance.

“As these capabilities grow more sophisticated and embedded in daily business processes, the division is intensifying its efforts to understand how the technologies influence outcomes,” the report states.

The SEC also warned that malicious actors are exploiting advanced AI to launch increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, including automated phishing campaigns and deepfake audio and video used to deceive employees and customers.

Examiners will assess whether financial institutions have adequately prepared for these threats and implemented safeguards against identity theft, account takeovers, and fraudulent transactions.

The agency also intends to scrutinize AI-powered trading algorithms and automated investment advice, particularly whether firms accurately describe their technologies and deliver recommendations consistent with investors’ financial objectives and risk profiles.

AI applications supporting fraud detection, anti-money laundering compliance, and back-office operations will also face examination. Meanwhile, the SEC said it is incorporating advanced AI into its own examination processes to improve efficiency, identify patterns and assess risks, while maintaining human oversight.

Quantum Computing Enters Regulatory Spotlight

Quantum computing also received explicit recognition as an emerging technology under Regulation SCI, although the SEC provided little detail about its specific concerns.

The inclusion is noteworthy as advances in quantum computing raise questions about the long-term security of cryptographic systems underpinning financial infrastructure.

For the cryptocurrency industry, sufficiently powerful quantum computers could eventually threaten the public-key cryptography used to secure Bitcoin and other blockchain networks, potentially necessitating upgrades to quantum-resistant alternatives.

The SEC did not directly connect quantum computing to cryptocurrency security or announce specific post-quantum requirements.

Beyond emerging technologies, the report emphasizes cybersecurity, third-party vendor oversight, investor protections, and coordination with other regulators, including the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

The document outlines examination priorities rather than new regulations, but its focus on tokenization, advanced AI, and quantum computing highlights the growing importance of technological resilience as traditional finance evolves.
